references.text: The Philistines brought the ark of the covenant to the temple of Dagon in Ashdod, showing how Dagon was worshiped as the chief god of the Philistines.
The hand of the Lord was heavy against the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors, demonstrating God's power over Dagon.
The Philistines captured Samson and gouged out his eyes, which is the immediate context for why they celebrated.
The people also praised their god Dagon for handing Samson over to them, continuing the theme of worshiping Dagon.
The Philistines placed Saul's armor in the temple of Dagon, showing that the worship of Dagon continued among the Philistines.
Israel served the gods of the Philistines, and the Lord sold them into the hands of the Philistines, a pattern repeated throughout the book of Judges.
God promised to execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt, demonstrating God's supremacy over pagan gods like Dagon.
